title: Christian Love and Devotion
english: The name of the Lord is proclaimed to all nations, and as a result, all nations are drawn to Him, bearing His name.
This phenomenon is evident because the young woman, like Paul, can confidently say, 'I can do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Philippians 4:13).
Therefore, she loves much, and her love is evident in her words, as she asks, 'Who will separate us from the love of Christ?' (Romans 8:35)
She answers this question by saying that she follows in His footsteps and enjoys the evangelical myrrh.
If we run with perseverance, guided by the word of the young women, we will follow the Lord God.
In the present circumstances, the storehouse can be seen as a kind of kingdom.
Perhaps she accuses herself of not guarding her own vineyard, allowing it to be destroyed by everyone passing by on the road, and thus failing to protect it from harm.
On the other hand, perhaps she also glorifies God because, although she was unable to guard her own vineyard, she was able to guard many other vineyards.

She is saying that the sons of her mother, the Synagogue, specifically the Scribes and Pharisees, who were fighting against those believing in Christ, are the ones who were supposed to be the vineyard, but they failed to fulfill their role.

However, she did not guard the vineyard, and for whatever gains she had, she considered them a loss for the sake of Christ, as the blessed Paul says, 'I consider them garbage, that I may gain Christ' (Philippians 3:7).
She is surrounded by the flocks of Christ's friends, who are the apostles, and He calls them friends, saying, 'I no longer call you slaves, but friends' (John 15:15).
As Paul said, 'until this day, when Moses is read, a veil lies on their heart' (2 Corinthians 3:15).

Paul also said, 'I can do all things in Christ who strengthens me' (Philippians 4:13), and 'Who will separate us from the love of Christ?' (Romans 8:35).
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmented and ends mid-sentence with 'a voice then, the', indicating a cut-off clause; no completion is attempted.
The translation of μῦρον ἐκκενωθὲν is literal, but the meaning may be metaphorical.
The word ἀγέλαις is translated as 'flocks', but it could also mean 'herds'.
The Bible references are based on the quotations and allusions in the text.
